body: NASA has successfully tested a navigation system that lets an aircraft identify hazardous terrain and change its landing approach, a capability being developed to help future spacecraft land safely on the Moon and Mars. The experiment used an Alta-X drone carrying NASA's Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) system, which performed simulated lunar descent and landing manoeuvres over Rogers Dry Lake near the agency's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, on 27 August. NASA announced the results on 4 November, saying the technology had demonstrated its ability to assess potential landing sites and guide a vehicle towards safer terrain.

SPLICE brings together navigation sensors, computers and guidance software designed to help a spacecraft determine where it is, identify obstacles and land accurately without relying entirely on instructions from Earth. Terrain-relative navigation uses a camera to photograph the surface and compare the images with maps previously obtained by orbiting spacecraft, while Navigation Doppler Lidar uses laser beams reflected from the surface to measure altitude and velocity, providing more precise measurements than conventional radar landing sensors while requiring less mass and power. Hazard Detection Lidar scans the terrain to produce a three-dimensional map, a descent and landing computer processes the sensor information to identify hazards and calculate a landing location, and adaptive guidance software can change the trajectory if the original site proves unsuitable. NASA says the hazard detection system is designed to begin scanning at an altitude of approximately 500 metres.

Development of SPLICE began in 2017, building on earlier NASA research into autonomous landing and hazard avoidance. The August demonstration followed several months of testing by engineers from NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston and Armstrong Flight Research Center, with Johnson developing the payload and Armstrong integrating it with the Alta-X drone; initial flights in June and July examined communications, telemetry, data handling and command-and-control functions, and a 15 July flight saw the payload communicate with the remotely piloted drone during hovering manoeuvres. Earlier work included sensor flights aboard Project Morpheus in 2014, Masten Space Systems' Xodiac rocket in 2017 and 2019, a rocket sled test of Navigation Doppler Lidar at speeds approaching 480 mph in June 2019, helicopter testing in March 2025, and closed-loop drone testing at Voyager Technologies' Lunar Surface Proving Grounds in Mojave, California, in August 2026. NASA is working with commercial lunar lander companies to incorporate SPLICE technologies into future spacecraft, and project manager Davis Adams said the team is coordinating with industry on use of the guidance system once it is available in the NASA software catalog, currently planned for this fall. NASA's project records list September 2026 as the SPLICE project closeout milestone.
en.summary: NASA has tested its SPLICE autonomous landing system aboard an Alta-X drone, flying simulated lunar descent and landing manoeuvres over Rogers Dry Lake in California on 27 August and announcing the results on 4 November. The system maps terrain during descent and can redirect a spacecraft to a safer site if the original target proves hazardous.
en.title: NASA tests autonomous Moon and Mars landing tech with SPLICE drone flight

body: NASA已成功測試一套導航系統，可讓飛行器辨識危險地形並改變著陸進場方式，協助未來太空船安全降落月球與火星。這次實驗使用搭載NASA安全精準著陸整合能力演進（SPLICE）系統的Alta-X無人機，8月27日在加州愛德華茲NASA阿姆斯壯飛行研究中心附近的羅傑斯乾湖上空執行模擬月球下降與著陸動作。NASA於11月4日公布結果，表示該技術已證明能評估潛在著陸點並引導飛行器前往較安全的地形。

SPLICE結合導航感測器、電腦與導引軟體，協助太空船在不完全依賴地球指令的情況下確認位置、辨識障礙物並精準著陸。其中地形相對導航以相機拍攝地面影像，再與軌道太空船先前取得的地圖比對；導航都卜勒光達以雷射反射測量高度與速度，NASA表示其測量比傳統雷達著陸感測器更精準，同時質量與耗電更低。危險偵測光達掃描地形並產生立體地圖，下降與著陸電腦處理感測器資訊、辨識危險並計算著陸位置，適應性導引軟體則能在原定著陸點不合適時改變軌跡。NASA表示，危險偵測系統設計為在約500公尺高度開始掃描地面。

SPLICE自2017年開始研發，奠基於NASA先前自主著陸與危險迴避研究。8月的展示飛行前，NASA詹森太空中心與阿姆斯壯飛行研究中心的工程師已進行數月測試，由詹森研發酬載、阿姆斯壯負責與Alta-X無人機整合；6月與7月的初期飛行測試通訊、遙測、資料處理與指揮管制功能，7月15日的飛行中酬載在無人機懸停時成功與遙控無人機通訊。先前工作包括2014年莫菲斯計畫火箭搭載感測器、2017年與2019年Masten太空系統Xodiac火箭測試、2019年6月以接近每小時480英里速度測試導航都卜勒光達的火箭橇實驗、2025年3月直升機測試，以及2026年8月在加州莫哈維航行者科技月球表面試驗場進行的閉迴路無人機測試。NASA正與商業月球著陸器公司合作，將SPLICE技術納入未來太空船；計畫經理戴維斯·亞當斯表示，團隊正與業界協調，待導引系統納入NASA軟體目錄後供業界使用，目前計畫於今年秋季完成。NASA計畫紀錄將2026年9月列為SPLICE計畫結案里程碑。
zh.summary: NASA以搭載SPLICE自主著陸系統的Alta-X無人機完成模擬月球下降與著陸測試，8月27日在加州羅傑斯乾湖上空飛行，11月4日公布結果。該系統能在下降過程中繪製地形圖，發現原定著陸點不安全時可改飛至較安全的地點。
zh.title: NASA以無人機測試SPLICE自主登月著陸技術
